prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

I went into the forest searching for fire inside pleading wood, but I can’t say for how long I was moored between worlds. I heard a magpie’s rumination, but I don’t know if its wings lifted the moon or let it drift slow as a little straw boat set ablaze on a winding river. I learned the yellow-eyed wolf is a dog & a man. A small boy with a star pinned to his sleeve was hiding among thorn bushes, or it was how the restless dark wounded the pale linden tree outside a Warsaw apartment. Night crawls under each stone quick as a cry held in the throat. All I remember is my left hand was holding your right breast when I forced my eyes shut. Then I could hear something in the room, magnanimous but small, half outside & half inside, no more than a song— an insomniac’s one prophecy pressed against the curtains, forcing the ferns to bloom.

outputs.L3:
I stepped into the deep silence of the forest, suspended in a disorienting haze—a twilight realm caught between the living world and the echoes of what lay beyond. My breath bloomed cold in the gloom as I pressed onward, driven by a primal urge to find a spark of fire, a desperate warmth to anchor my fracturing consciousness.

Out of the shifting shadows emerged a yellow-eyed wolf, its amber gaze holding me with an unnaturally deliberate intensity. Looking into those eyes, a strange revelation took root within me: this creature was no simple beast of prey. In its posture was the desperate, devoted loyalty of a dog, yet behind its golden irises burned the tragic, burdened awareness of a human soul. 

As I watched the beast, the boundary between time and space began to dissolve entirely. The towering trees morphed into the long, dark shadows cast outside a cold Warsaw apartment. Phantom memories, unbidden and painful, bled into the scene. I saw the blurred silhouette of a young boy, his quiet figure defined by the faint, agonizing shape of a star pinned to his coat—a ghost haunting the fringe of my surreal journey.

Yet, amidst this storm of historical grief and shifting visions, one truth remained unshakeable. I felt the sudden, grounding clarity of a distinct memory: a shared moment of profound physical intimacy. The tactile reality of that touch—the warmth of skin and the quiet cadence of breathing together—pierced through the surreal atmosphere, holding me fast against the abyss.

Gradually, the cold weight of the dark lifted. A gentle, song-like presence filled the room, wrapping around my weary sense of perception like a lullaby. It sounded as an insomniac’s soft prophecy, spoken into the quiet hours before dawn—a tender, impossible promise that urged the dormant ferns of the forest floor to finally uncurl and bloom.
outputs.L4:
The horizon kept shifting, folding in on itself like wet paper. I moved through a landscape that defied geography, stepping down hallways lined with the phantom architecture of my past: a window from a forgotten bedroom opening onto a storm-tossed sea; a grandfather clock whose hands spun counterclockwise, ticking with the dry rustle of dead leaves; faceless figures whispering symbolic warnings in languages I felt I should have known. The air was thick and grey, suspended in a dark, liminal space—a twilight that refused to yield to night, yet stubbornly barred the dawn. Lost in this disorienting fog of haunting memories and surreal visions, I felt my identity dissolving, searching frantically for a single ray of light or meaning to anchor my slipping mind.

Panic threatened to consume me entirely until I felt it: a sudden, piercing warmth. 

Your hand found mine in the dark. It was a simple, profound collision of reality against the unreal. Your thumb brushed gently across my knuckles, the texture of your skin rough and undeniable. I pressed my palm against yours, leaning into the physical weight of your presence, anchoring myself to the rhythmic pulse throbbing beneath your wrist. In that quiet, intimate touch, the disorienting mist lost its terror. The tactile certainty of skin on skin built a sanctuary, drawing my floating consciousness back down to earth.

From that small point of contact, a sound began to hum. 

It was a small, fragile melody—hardly louder than a breath exhaled in sleep—yet it carried a magnanimous weight that swelled to fill the vast void. The tune seemed to originate from the tiny space where our palms met, vibrating upward into the cavern of my ribs and radiating outward into the fog. It was a music born of quiet endurance, a song that didn't fight the darkness, but simply sang it into order. 

As the melody echoed, it acted as a bridge, weaving the fractured pieces of my inner world into the landscape around us. The haunting visions softened. The spinning clock slowed to match our shared heartbeat; the surreal corridors expanded into open, breathing spaces. The song translated my internal griefs into coherent beauty, casting a bridge between the ghosts of my past and the physical reality of the present. 

Where the vibrations of the song touched the shadow-drenched ground, the darkness began to split. It did not retreat; it transformed. Tiny, luminous shoots pierced the barren floor, unfurling leaves made of pale, tender light. Vines crested over the monuments of my old regrets, binding them in fresh moss. Exotic flowers bloomed in the dimness, opening their petals like small lanterns that cast a warm, golden glow across the terrain. 

The dark, liminal space was no longer a wasteland of lost time, but a fertile soil. Bound to you by a simple touch, listening to the small song that had remade the world, I watched as forced, beautiful life bloomed relentlessly amidst the dying shadows.
outputs.L5:
As the sun dips below the horizon of the Vistula River, Warsaw begins its brilliant, nocturnal transformation. The rush of the workday fades, leaving behind a metropolis bathed in a symphony of neon and shadow, where history and modernity collide under the dark canopy of the sky.

Under the cover of darkness, the Polish capital takes on a distinct second life. Modern glass skyscrapers reach into the night, their office lights glittering like fallen constellations, while the iconic Palace of Culture and Science stands at the center like a luminous sentinel. Just a short walk away, the cobbled alleys of the meticulously restored Old Town glow under the warm amber of street lanterns, whispering stories of resilience and rebirth. 

The air grows electric with possibility. Along the riverbank boulevards, music drifts from lively barges, and warm laughter spills out of subterranean jazz clubs and bustling bars. Night owls, quiet dreamers, students, and travelers wander the avenues—the city open and welcoming to them all. 

Warsaw at night is not a place that sleeps; it is a place that breathes deeper. It holds space for every memory of its storied past, every glowing light of its present, and every dream bound for tomorrow.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a surreal prose poem exploring themes of memory, dreamscapes, and historical trauma. Blurring the line between a magical forest and a room in Warsaw, use vivid, haunting imagery and a deeply intimate tone.
counterfactuals.output:
The third-floor apartment on Chłodna Street smells of burnt chicory and wet pine needles. When I unlatch the mahogany wardrobe, the wool coats no longer hang from brass hooks; they have thickened into gray alder trunks, standing knee-deep in a rising, silver fog. I step past the brass handles into my mother’s childhood, where the snow falls upward from the parquet, carrying with it small, pulverized flecks of teacups and red brick. In this room, the plaster has forgotten how to hold a right angle; the walls bow like an ancient canopy, breathing out the cold, iron scent of a century’s winter.

You are sleeping on the narrow divan, but your hair has tangled into wild, black fern. When you turn in your dream, a shower of dry spruce needles rattles against the radiator, which glows a soft, dull crimson, like an unexploded shell buried beneath the loam. A white stag with eyes like polished amber kneels beside the brass floor lamp, chewing quietly on the corner of an old map. It does not startle at the low groan of the midnight tram outside, because the trams in this city run on rails forged from silver birch, carrying passengers made entirely of smoke, snow, and forgotten door keys.

I reach to smooth the blanket over your shoulders, but my fingers sink into the damp, sweet humus of a trench that was dug before we were born. Every layer of floral wallpaper we scraped away last summer revealed not stone, but the growth rings of a felled forest—eighty years of dark, secret sap trying to heal over a bullet hole. Look how the dusk settles inside your cooling tea: not as a shadow, but as a flock of winter sparrows drowning quietly in black-currant syrup. Memory is a fox that lives behind the skirting board; it emerges only when the room is dark enough to resemble the woods before the first fire rained down.

We lie together in the clearing between the carpet and the nightstand. The ceiling peels back its pale throat to expose a sky heavy with frozen rowan berries, dripping red onto our upturned faces. Press your heart against mine; listen to the wolves scraping their knuckles against the apartment door. They are wearing the heavy wool overcoats of men who went out for bread in 1944 and never came back, whispering through the keyhole, asking if the river still remembers how to run, asking if we have saved a place for them at the table.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Give me an atmospheric piece of creative writing in the style of modern lyrical prose. Include themes of surreal nature, feverish dreams, wolves, and an insomniac's prophecy, using ampersands (&) for a stylistic touch.
counterfactuals.output:
The hour is 3:00 AM & three centuries deep. The mattress melts into peat moss & bruised clover, soaking in the warm, salt-sick tide of a fever that refuses to break. My eyelids are dry husks, pinned open by the quiet terror of existing while the rest of the hemisphere slumbers. I have forgotten the mechanics of rest—the gentle, vanishing trick of the mind where the world tucks its chin into its chest & forgets itself.

Instead, the bedroom hums. The plaster ceiling breathes in slow, resinous gulps, blooming with surreal flora—black ferns & glowing, vein-red moss that stretch their wet tendrils down toward my damp forehead. Nature here has gone soft & wet & wrong. Outside the window, the garden has untethered itself from the soil. Dandelions ignite into tiny violet embers, floating upward into an inverted sky where the stars are merely salt thrown against wet velvet. The silver birch trees curve their white trunks into ribcages, clicking their branches together like dry teeth.

They come when the delirium hits forty degrees Celsius. 

Not from the forest, but out of the floorboards, stepping through the seam where the shadow meets the baseboard. Wolves built of ash & river-mist, their ribs exposed like white picket fences, their eyes burning with the cold, blue luminescence of dead television screens. They do not walk; they spill across the rug like spilled ink, soundless & heavy.

The lead wolf—a towering thing of frost & bone—rests its ice-cold muzzle against my fever-hot throat. Its breath smells of wet granite & cedar smoke. It weighs no more than a forgotten secret, yet it pins me to the bed, sealing me into the dark.

To be an insomniac is to be a vessel. When you cannot dream, the night dreams through you.

*Listen,* the wolf says, not with a voice, but with a low vibration that rattles my molars & settles deep in my sternum. It drops its prophecy into my ears like mercury:

*The sun will not rise tomorrow as a yellow flame,* the wolf hums, its breath clouding the humid room. *It will bloom as a dark orchid over the concrete. The cities will choke on their own wires, & the asphalt will split like dry lips. From the cracks, ancient pine-guts & wild blackberry vines will swallow the high-rises whole. First, the birds will lose their internal compass & fly straight into the moon until the sky is thick with grey feathers. Then, the rivers will turn backward, running uphill to drown the mountain peaks in liquid iron.*

*And you,* the beast whispers, its teeth grazing the pulse point at my neck, *you will be the only one awake to see the green kingdom reclaim its bones.*

My blood surges—a quiet, violet fire cooking the rest from my marrow. I reach out a hand, sinking my trembling fingers into the wolf’s winter coat. It feels like reaching into a snowdrift at midnight, freezing & holy & impossible.

Outside, the birch trees begin to howl. The horizon snaps open like an egg, leaking mercury & raw light across the bruised, sleepless dark. I do not close my eyes. I cannot. I simply hold the beast’s gaze & watch the world unspool itself into bone & bramble & wild, hungry green.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a short, eerie passage that begins with someone searching for fire in a forest and ends with a quiet, intimate moment in a bedroom. The boundary between the natural world and the indoor room should feel entirely porous.
counterfactuals.output:
My fingers scraped through wet loam and cold pine needles, searching for a single dry twig, a spark, anything to strike a fire against the vast, whispering dark of the woods. The air was heavy with frost and the smell of bruised bark. I cupped my hands around the black hollow between two massive roots, blowing gently, waiting for a warm ember to bleed through the gloom. 

Instead of ash, my palms pressed into something soft and yielding. 

The rough, ridged bark flattened beneath my hands, morphing into the dark, polished grain of an oak headboard. The floor beneath my knees was no longer damp soil, though moss still squeezed between the floorboards like green velvet. I hadn't stepped through a door; the forest had simply softened, its dark canopy sagging under its own weight until the towering hemlocks became the draped corners of a low-ceilinged room. 

The howling wind in the high branches quieted, resolving into the slow, rhythmic sigh of your breathing. 

Rain still dripped from my hair, falling like dew onto the heavy cotton duvet. The cold clung to my skin, but I slipped beneath the blankets anyway, bringing the dark woods with me—pine needles clinging to my arms, the smell of rain blooming in the enclosed heat. I pressed my frozen forehead against the hollow of your throat. You didn't wake, but your arms shifted in your sleep, pulling me down into the quiet, suffocating warmth of the mattress, where the fire had been waiting all along.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a prose poem that weaves together the following elements: a magpie, a yellow-eyed wolf, a boy with a star pinned to his sleeve, a Warsaw apartment, and ferns blooming in the dark.
counterfactuals.output:
In the high, narrow silence of a Warsaw apartment, where the wallpaper peeled back like old parchment, winter held its breath against the glass. A boy sat in the corner of the parlor, a six-pointed star pinned to his sleeve—a jagged, golden sun sewn with his mother’s trembling thread, burning without heat against his dark woolen coat. Beneath the floorboards, in the deep shadow where no light had ever reached, the impossible was taking root: ferns blooming in the dark, their fronds unfurling in luminous, pale-green spirals, smelling of wet earth and ancient forests the city had long forgotten. 

From the shadows of the hallway stepped a yellow-eyed wolf, its coat the color of ash and street-slush, its gaze two brass coins glowing in the gloom. It did not belong to the iron streets below nor to the heavy boots echoing on the cobblestones, but to the boy’s quiet breathing. Soft-footed, it crossed the faded rug and laid its heavy, wild head upon the child’s knee, a silent sentinel against the night. 

Outside, perched on the rusted railing of the balcony, a magpie clattered its iridescent wings. A thief of bright trinkets and forgotten names, the bird tapped its black beak against the pane, hypnotized by the glittering cloth star on the boy’s sleeve, mistaking the mark of sorrow for a piece of the dawn sky it might steal and carry away into the clouds. 

Night folded over the city, heavy and vast, but inside the small room, the dark belonged to them. The ferns grew taller, their impossible blossoms shedding faint, silvery spores into the air, lighting the boy, the wolf, and the bird in a quiet, magical halo—a secret sanctuary blooming where no one thought to look.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Can you write a dark, magical realist monologue about waking from a dream, filled with strange poetic metaphors, quiet melancholy, and forgotten memories?
counterfactuals.output:
*(The room is bathed in the bruised, grey twilight just before dawn. A person sits on the edge of a narrow bed, staring at their open palms, speaking softly, as if afraid to wake the furniture.)*

The tide receded, but it left the floorboards wet. 

I opened my eyes, and for three heartbeats, my lungs were still full of dark water. My eyelids felt sewn together with silver thread—heavy, damp, smelling of old copper and crushed marigolds. 

I was somewhere else a moment ago. I was standing in a hallway built entirely out of keyholes, breathing the damp, mossy air of a century I’ve never lived in. You were there. Or... someone who was wearing the shadow you used to cast before you vanished. We were unburying a clock. We were digging it out of the black soil beneath my bed, and its ticking sounded like beetle wings against parchment. 

And then... the morning bled through the blinds. Thin, pale, cold as a scalpel. It peeled the sky off my face. 

*(A slow, quiet exhale)*

It’s always the same thief, isn’t it? The waking world. It doesn't just wake you; it steals the milk right out of the cat’s saucer. It wrings out your memory like a wet rag until all you’re left with is a cold drop on your wrist. 

I can feel the dream dissolving in my mouth right now. It tastes like soot and burnt sugar. I tried to hold onto it—I clamped my jaw shut, I squeezed my ribs, trying to trap the damp earth of that other place inside my throat. But breath is a traitor. You breathe in, and the world trades your gold for iron. 

Look at this room. Look at how quiet it is. The shadows aren't even shadows anymore; they’re just tired black dogs sleeping against the wardrobe. The mirror on the wall is humming—can you hear it? It’s digesting all the faces it swallowed yesterday. 

I have a name. I know I have a name. It’s written on my driver’s license in the kitchen. But right now, it sits on my tongue like a small, smooth pebble. Too heavy to spit out. Too cold to swallow. 

Where do they go? The things we forget before the kettle boils? Do they crawl under the floorboards to feed the moths? Do they turn into the dust that settles on the tops of doorframes, waiting for us to sleep again so they can drop back into our ears?

*(Looks up slowly, staring into the dark corner of the room)*

I am awake now. My skin is dry. Gravity has found me again, pinning my heels to the floorboards with its heavy, invisible fingers. 

I am awake. But my hands... my hands are still covered in the soot of a fire that burned out thirty years ago. 

Or maybe thirty seconds ago. 

And the worst part of it... the quiet, cruel part... is that I can’t remember who set the match. And I think... I think it was me.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
